SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND ADDL.
MACT AT BIDAR IN MVC NO.613/2017.

THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed by the claimants seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional MACT, Bidar (henceforth referred to as 'Tribunal') in MVC No.613/2017 vide its judgment and award dated 13.08.2020.

2. The claimants are the dependant legal heirs of the deceased - Kasturibai, who was aged 40 years and who died in a road traffic accident on 03.08.2016 involving an autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA-38-7444 (henceforth referred to as 'offending vehicle').
The claimants claimed that the deceased was a domestic help and was earning a monthly income of Rs.15,000/-.

The claimants claimed that due to the death of NC: 2023:KHC-K:5514 Smt. Kasturibai, they had lost the financial and emotional support and hence, filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation from the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.
3. The claim petition was resisted by the insurer of the offending vehicle who denied the accident as well as the entitlement of the claimants for compensation.
The insurer contended that the claimants had colluded with the owner of the offending vehicle and the police and registered a false case against the offending vehicle to claim compensation.

It further contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess a valid licence to drive the vehicle and therefore, there was a violation of conditions of policy and hence, the insurer was exonerated from its liability to indemnify the owner.
Drauipati W/O Sambappa @ Sambanna vs Suresh Gaikwad S/O Kallappa Gaikwad And ... on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167716882/
2 4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant No.1 was examined as PW.1 and she marked Exs.P1 to P6.
The insurer did not lead any evidence.

5. Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the driver of the offending vehicle was rash NC: 2023:KHC-K:5514 and negligent and was solely responsible for the accident resulting in the death of Smt. Kasturibai.

It held that the deceased was aged 45 years and considered her notional income at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and deducted 1/2 towards her personal and living expenses and applied multiplier of '14' and factored the loss of future prospects at 25% and awarded the following compensation:-
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Loss of dependency 6,30,000/-
 2 Loss of estate 15,000/-
 3 Funeral expenses 15,000/-
 Total 6,60,000/-
The Tribunal directed the insurer of the offending vehicle to pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realisation.
6. Being not satisfied with the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimants are in appeal.
7.

The learned counsel for the claimants contended that the Tribunal committed an error in considering the notional NC: 2023:KHC-K:5514 income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month while in similar circumstances, the notional income is considered at a sum of Rs.8,750/- per month.
He further contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal under other heads was also meager and the same deserves to be enhanced.
8. Per contra, the learned counsel for the insurer contended that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and does not warrant any enhancement.
9. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimants and the learned counsel for the insurer.

10. As rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimants, the Tribunal must have considered the notional income of the deceased at a sum of Rs.8,750/- per month as per the Chart prescribed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for settlement of claims at Lok Adalat.
The claimants are also entitled to loss of future prospects at 25% and deduction towards personal and living expenses at  of the income.

3 11.

Consequently, the claimants are entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:-
 Sl. Particulars Amount  No. (in Rs.)
 1 Towards loss of dependency 9,18,792/-
 2 Towards loss of consortium 40,000/-
 3 Towards loss of estate and 30,000/-
funeral
expenses etc.,

Since the liability of the insurer is undisputed, it shall pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the claim petition till the date of realisation.
13. In view of the above, the appeal is allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.6,60,000/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.9,88,792/-, which is payable by the insurer along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
14.

The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal NC: 2023:KHC-K:5514 within a period of one month from the date of receipt of certified copy of this Judgment.
15. Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant No.1 in any nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
